title: Add the mask
starter:
%x  = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=0
%w  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=2
%i  = range 6
%yv = shrink %y %i []
%z  = store %yv 0
%y0 = after %y %z
%k  = range 3
%ik = add %i %k
%j  = add %ik -1
%jm = mod %j 6
%xv = shrink %x %jm []
%xe = load %xv
%wv = shrink %w %k []
%we = load %wv
%p  = mul %xe %we
%yv0 = shrink %y0 %i []
%cur = load %yv0
%sum = add %cur %p
%s  = store %yv0 %sum
%ek = end %s %k
%ei = end %ek %i
%y1 = after %y %ei
hints: The starter wraps around: at `i = 0` the left tap reads `x[5]`, and at `i = 5` the right tap reads `x[0]`. Those two reads should count as 0.
`j` is a real index exactly when `0 <= j` and `j < 6`. Build that bool from two `cmplt` lines: `cmplt %j 0` is true off the left end, and `cmplt %j 6` is false off the right end.

Add `%lo = cmplt %j 0`, `%hi = cmplt %j 6` and `%ok = where %lo false %hi`. After the load, add `%xz = where %ok %xe 0` and multiply `%xz`, not `%xe`, by the kernel element. Keep `mod %j 6` as the offset.
explain: The offset stays `mod j 6`, which is provably in [0, 5], so every view is legal. The new `where` swaps the loaded element for 0 whenever `j` is -1 or 6, so the element that the wrapped offset picked up never reaches the sum. The test with a 1 at one end shows the wrap most clearly: without the mask it leaks to the other end.
